question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (2)
solution:
The correct answer is '**on**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The passage mentions remembering Sudama and Krishna on a specific occasion, which is the auspicious day of Friendship. 
 
• The appropriate preposition should indicate a specific day or date. 
 
• "**On**" fits well as it is used to denote specific days and dates, such as "on Friendship Day." 
 
• Other options ("**at**", "**in**", "**over**") do not fit the context of specifying a particular day. 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: * The two, Sudama and Krishna, were (1) **inseparable**__. To date, their oneness is an example of true friendship ahead of the planet. This is often the rationale why they are remembered (2) __**on**__ the auspicious day of Friendship. Even after losing touch for several years after finishing their studies together, they did not (3) _______ the hope of meeting again. Sudama always had lord Krishna in his heart and soul and kept (4) _______ of him until they met again. The entire incident when Sudama met Krishna after numerous years is so (5) _______ and unforgettable. * 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** __Additional Information__ ** 

 
• At (पर): "At" is used to indicate a specific place or a point in time but is not typically used for specific dates or days. 
 
• In (में): "In" is used for unspecific times during a day, month, season, or year, but not for particular days. 
 
• Over (के ऊपर): "Over" is typically used to indicate a period of time, but not a specific day or occasion.
